stories.summary: Record-low water levels on the Danube forced the Paks plant offline, leaving Hungary facing a potential power crunch.

He made the announcement on social media late Saturday night, saying the decision was taken after a further drop in the Danube's water level . The plant, located 120 kilometers (74.5 miles) south of the capital, Budapest, uses water from the Danube to cool its reactors. It provides more than 40% of Hungary's electricity generation. Record-low Danube levels necessitated the shutdown The Danube has fallen to record-low levels in some areas after months of below-average rainfall and successive heat waves since May. "There's always a bit of adrenaline when you get the call," marine firefighter Julien says. "But we're trained; we're prepared." Maitre Julien — whom DW can only identity by rank and first name — is part of Marseille-based battalion deployed to France's Gironde region to tackle a wildfire which prompted the largest evacuations in the country since World War II. stories.article_text_excerpt: Crowds line Amsterdam's canals for Pride boat parade Crowds line Amsterdam's canals for Pride boat parade Close Amsterdam came alive with music, colour and celebration on Saturday, as thousands of people flocked to the canals to watch the city's annual Pride boat parade. The Dutch capital is hosting this years' WorldPride event, drawing visitors from across the world. Costumed participants danced and waved from a colourful flotilla of 80 decorated vessels as they made their way through the city's waterways. Security was visibly heightened at the event, with police cruising the canals in motorboats. stories.article_text_excerpt: Image source, Getty Images By Robert Greenall Published 1 August 2026 Updated 1 hour ago At least three people have been killed and 21 injured after a homemade explosive device was detonated at an Italian restaurant in Moscow, Russian state media quotes security officials as saying. The blast happened at around 20:00 local time (17:00 GMT) on Kudrinskaya square near the city centre. The National Anti-Terrorist Committee (NAK) said a woman carrying the explosives tried to enter the restaurant but was stopped by a security guard. The device detonated, killing the woman, the guard and a visitor to the restaurant. The restaurant, located in one of Moscow's famous Stalin-era skyscrapers, had been holding a private function. Authorities have not disclosed the guest list or said anything about who they believe was the target of the attack. Witnesses said they saw people being brought out covered in blood after the explosion. Initial reports said the blast happened in the establishment's kitchen but the restaurant later issued a statement saying "there was a problem outside". Roads around the square were briefly closed. stories.title: Germany's long road to equality for same-sex couples
stories.summary: In 2001, same-sex couples in Germany were able to register a civil partnership for the first time. The Civil Partnership Act was a crucial step toward "marriage for all," which was introduced in 2017.

However, another 16 years would pass before marriage itself became an option. "The Civil Partnership Act was a milestone for the legal recognition of same-sex couples in Germany and laid the foundation for opening up marriage," Alexander Vogt of the national board of " Queere Vielfalt e.V. " (Queer diversity) told DW. "It introduced a legally secure partnership with rights similar to those of marriage — such as inheritance, maintenance, and residency rights — though it remained discriminatory in many areas – like adoption or tax law. Nevertheless, it gave us a foot in the door — a solid base from which further rights could be secured, usually by appealing to the Federal Constitutional Court ." The US Geological Survey measured it at magnitude 6.8. The Japanese prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, said rescue workers faced a “race against time” to reach more people still trapped in rubble. “We will go all out to find and rescue as many people as we can,” she said. stories.title: Iran rejects Hormuz deal and launches surprise strike on US forces in Jordan
stories.summary: Tehran rejected an Omani proposal to divide the strait equally and declared Hormuz would "never return to its prewar situation," hours before the IRGC launched multiple ballistic missiles at US forces in Jordan in what CENTCOM called an attempted surprise attack.
